subject: mathematics
question_text: If f(x) = 2x − 1 and g(x) = x², find (√f/g)(x).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.11, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 16(iii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards the rule √(2x − 1)/x² first and the domain, from the root and the denominator together, second. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find (√f/g)(x) — the rule, and every condition x must satisfy for it to be defined.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the rule
steps.margin_note: First mark. The square root acts on f alone, and that root is then divided by g(x) = x².

recall.must_convey: That (√f/g)(x) = √(2x − 1)/x², with the root taken of f only.
accept: root f over g is root of two x minus one divided by x squared
the square root applies to f only
root two x minus one on top and x squared below
root f pina x square kinda untundi
write root of two x minus one over x squared

steps.why: √f is the function whose value at x is √(f(x)), and dividing by g divides that value by g(x). Writing the rule this way shows the root is not taken of the whole fraction.
steps.memory_tip: √f/g means the root of f on top, g underneath: √(2x − 1)/x².
common_mistakes: Taking the square root of the whole fraction, writing √((2x − 1)/x²).
Reading √f/g as √(f/g) and cancelling inside the root.

steps.label: Find where it is defined
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two conditions must be checked: the root needs 2x − 1 ≥ 0 and the denominator needs x ≠ 0. Together they give x ≥ 1/2.
lines: x² in the denominator needs x ≠ 0.
Every x ≥ 1/2 is already non zero, so the

recall.must_convey: That 2x − 1 ≥ 0 gives x ≥ 1/2, that x² ≠ 0 gives x ≠ 0, and that both together give the domain [1/2, ∞).
accept: the root needs two x minus one at least zero so x is at least one half
x squared in the denominator cannot be zero so x is not zero
both conditions together give x greater than or equal to one half
root ki two x minus one zero kanna thakkuva undakoodadu, x half kanna ekkuva
the domain is one half to infinity

steps.why: A quotient with a square root carries two separate restrictions, and both have to be written. Here x ≥ 1/2 already rules out x = 0, so the domain is [1/2, ∞).
steps.memory_tip: Check the root and the denominator separately, then keep the values that satisfy both. Here x ≥ 1/2 already covers x ≠ 0.
common_mistakes: Giving the rule with no domain, so the answer is stated where the function does not exist.
Checking the root only and forgetting that x² cannot be 0.
Writing x > 1/2 instead of x ≥ 1/2 — at x = 1/2 the root is 0, which is allowed.
